items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Inez Cavanaugh, the wife of Timmie Rosenkrantz who had been my manager... There were four people in Los Angeles that I had known back East

ctx.x: We played two weeks in the big hall and then went downstairs in a smaller club called the "Pingoin". Adelaide Hall did an attraction. The band also sang some spiritual numbers with Willie always singing the lead. Willie had a wonderful baritone voice and sang with great power. The "Pingoin" was more suited for a jazz orchestra than the big hall upstairs, but we had success in both places.

Benny Carter had a vacation from his job in the B.B.C. so he and his wife Inez came to Knocke, but Benny was on holiday and never sat in with the band although he came to the club often. Another famous

Negro woman who was an opera singer and had sang in the casino was Miss Catherine Yarbo. I saw Catherine when she did Aida in Knocke and she was a great artist. She had her vacation after playing the casino and stayed in Knocke for two weeks. She did not know how to ride a bicycle so she and another woman friend of hers rented a four wheeled pedal contraption and rode to Sluis or Seebrugge with us.
